name: Onboard new hires from BambooHR to Slack, Jira and DocuSign with Claude

parameters.content:
## Onboard new hires from BambooHR to Slack, Jira and DocuSign with Claude

HR and people-ops teams that build every new hire's checklist, accounts and paperwork by hand.

### How it works
Trigger: BambooHR, Rippling, Workday or Personio announces the moment a candidate's status becomes Hired; for platforms that cannot, the workflow checks the HRIS every hour.
1. Receive the new-hire event
2. Build the checklist for this role
3. Create the tracking board
4. Request accounts and equipment
5. Send documents for signature
6. Schedule the first two weeks
7. Run the welcome sequence
8. Answer policy questions
9. Chase overdue tasks and check in
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus BambooHR / Rippling / Workday, Notion / Jira / Google Sheets, DocuSign / PandaDoc.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Edit the role-to-checklist mapping in the Config node and add your own account-provisioning nodes (Okta, Google Workspace) after the approval step.
Guardrail to keep: The AI agent answers only from the handbook and cites the page; it refuses pay, performance and grievance topics and routes them to HR.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/employee-onboarding-automation/

## 1. Receive the new-hire event
The HRIS posts the new employee record: name, role, department, start date, manager, location

## 2. Build the checklist for this role
A role → checklist map (kept in a Google Sheet or Notion database so HR can edit it without touching the workflow) defines the tasks, owners and due dates relative to the start date: paperwork, equipment, accounts, training modules, introductions

nodes.name: Section: 2. Build the checklist for this role

parameters.content:
## 3. Create the tracking board
One page per hire with every task, owner and due date

## 4. Request accounts and equipment
Creates the IT tickets (Jira Service Management, ServiceNow, Freshservice) for laptop, email, SSO groups and role-specific tools, pre-filled from the HRIS record so IT never has to ask

## 5. Send documents for signature
Generates the contract, NDA and policy acknowledgements from templates and sends them via DocuSign or PandaDoc

## 6. Schedule the first two weeks
Books the manager 1:1, team introductions, IT setup slot and mandatory training from the checklist, inviting the right people with the right context

nodes.name: Section: 6. Schedule the first two weeks

parameters.content:
## 7. Run the welcome sequence
Day −7, −1, 1, 7 and 30 emails, personalised from the record: what to expect, who to meet, where things are

## 8. Answer policy questions
A Slack bot backed by an AI Agent node with your handbook in a vector store

## 9. Chase overdue tasks and check in
A daily run compares the board to today's date, nudges owners of overdue items, and sends the 30/60/90-day check-in survey to the hire and the manager

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Answer policy questions" step of the Employee Onboarding Automation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: A Slack bot backed by an AI Agent node with your handbook in a vector store. It answers PTO, benefits, expenses and equipment questions with citations to the handbook page, and hands anything about pay, performance or complaints to HR.

Rules:
- The AI agent answers only from the handbook and cites the page; it refuses pay, performance and grievance topics and routes them to HR.
- Account provisioning is requested, never executed, by the workflow — IT approves in their own tool.
- Personal data stays in the HRIS; the workflow passes identifiers, not copies of documents.
- Every automated message is logged on the hire's board so HR can see exactly what was sent.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Answer policy questions
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.
